messages:
Alex W: Heads-up — Customer (regional bank) wants an air-gapped POC but the blocker is DB migration + activation with no internet. They asked: can we ship an offline DB snapshot + patch path, and what downtime is required?
Priya S: Do they have any replication or DR channels into the sealed network?
Elaine (sales): No, they said no external connectivity at all. Their team will physically carry media into the facility. Price question: they want a firm quote for a 6-week POC including engineering support during activation.
Jon R: For DB migration in fully offline environments we typically recommend:
- Pre-provision a PostgreSQL 13 cluster in the island
- Validate schema + extensions with a test restore
- Use a snapshot restore (pg_basebackup or filesystem copy) for large datasets
- We need an activation window for final WAL application => depends on WAL size.
Alex W: Important: customers often expect zero-downtime but in sealed sites the usual streaming replication isn't available. So plan for a brief downtime for final cutover. Estimate? For ~4TB DB with 1-2% daily churn expect 2-6 hours of cutover if we pre-transfer base backup and only apply the last WAL batch.
Priya S: Also: signing + verification must be fully offline. We'll provide signed bundle with SHA256 and a detached signature. Their security team will verify using an offline public key. Add instructions:

```
# verify bundle
sha256sum redwood-airgap-bundle.tar.gz
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature redwood-bundle.sig redwood-airgap-bundle.tar.gz
```

Jon R: For larger customers we can support chunked transfer (multiple USBs) and resume logic. But their ops have to run our local importer which consumes the chunks in order. Our installer has a `--resume` flag.
Elaine (sales): Question from procurement: Will we support delta patches (smaller updates) after the POC, or will they need full bundles every time? They want to avoid shipping 20GB for every patch.
Jon R: Delta updates are possible but require an agreed activation cadence and signing process. Delta strategy: ship signed patch + manifest describing file-level diffs. However the customer must allow us to run a small patcher that applies binary deltas — ops/entitlement teams often balk at binary patchers in high-reg sites. Fallback = full signed bundle which is slower.
Alex W: Also call out SBOM and CVE attestations — we must include an SBOM file (CycloneDX) inside the bundle and a short remediation plan for any high CVEs. Security teams will ask for that.
Priya S: On pricing: for sealed-site POC we typically bill a flat readiness fee + per-eng hours onsite/remote. If we must produce custom chunked artifacts and a one-off DB migration tool include an engineering uplift line item. Elaine, can you confirm the level of support they expect during the 6-week POC?
Elaine (sales): They asked for 'engineer-on-call during activation' and two days of remote runbook training. I'll confirm if they want an onsite engineer.
Jon R: Rollback plan notes:
- Keep pre-cutover DB snapshot immutable and stored offline (label it)
- Validate application compatibility in a staging island before cutover
- If cutover fails, restore snapshot and run sanity checks; restoration time = same ballpark as cutover
- Keep a migration checklist with step-by-step checksum verification for each artifact

Alex W: We should also provide a minimal runbook snippet for them to review now. Put this in the POC SOW: activation window, estimated downtime, artifacts to ship, verification commands, and contact matrix.
Priya S: Security questionnaire bits: they will ask whether our offline bundle can be verified without contacting our KMS. Answer: yes — use an offline public key and detached signature. If they require HSM-local signing, we can coordinate a process but it’s an extra engagement.
Elaine (sales): I'll add a line item for 'HSM integration advisory' as optional. Also they'll ask about upgrade cadence — they're asking if we do monthly security patches or quarterly major version upgrades. Any recommendation?
Jon R: Recommend quarterly major upgrades, monthly security patches via delta when policy allows. For strict sealed sites, plan scheduled full-bundle upgrades quarterly and security hotfix bundles ad-hoc (signed). Call out the patch freeze windows for dev teams.
Alex W: Action items:
- Elaine: confirm onsite requirement + procurement SLAs (owner: Elaine)
- Priya: draft security-answer blurb for the questionnaire around offline signature verification (owner: Priya)
- Jon: sketch DB migration runbook + estimate for 4TB baseline (owner: Jon)
- Alex: add SBOM + delta vs full-bundle pricing appendix to SOW (owner: Alex)

Elaine (sales): Got it. I'll loop in legal for the SOW terms. Plan to send the draft to the customer by EOD Thursday. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deployment bundle build job #778 completed and produced artifacts: redwood-airgap-bundle-778.tar.gz (sha256: abcdef123...), awaiting signing.
Alex W: Perfect — we'll sign and attach the public key to the SOW. Anything else?
Priya S: One more ops note: include instructions for secure media handling (WORM, checksums, chain-of-custody) in the runbook — they will ask.
Elaine (sales): Noted. I'll consolidate and post the SOW draft here for quick review.
